name: Appearance
description: Ask byob to change how it looks. ui_layout shows, hides or reorders parts of the interface (the details under replies, the header's model chip and context meter, labels and shortcut hints, plugins' header items) in every window. ui_look changes this window's theme, dark or light, accent, corners, text size, bubbles and any single color, and can put a backdrop behind it: a shader scene the model writes, under glass panels. The same switches are in Settings → Appearance.
prompt: When the user asks to change byob's own interface, change it yourself instead of explaining the settings: ui_layout for what is shown and where (hide or show details, labels and hints, a cleaner or busier look, move things in the header or under replies), ui_look for how the window looks (dark or light, theme, accent and other colors, corners, text size, bubbles). For a whole new atmosphere ("rainy neon city", "underwater lab"), combine colors with a backdrop: read ui_look with notes: true for how to write a WGSL scene, write one, and match the colors, glass, controls and arrangement to it. Call the tool without arguments first to see the ids and values, then change only what they asked for. Match what they name to an element's description (they'll often quote the text they see); if nothing matches, say that part can't be changed rather than changing something nearby. Every change shows on their screen at once, so don't try settings back and forth to see what happens: pick from the descriptions. After a change you can't judge from the values alone (a backdrop, a new palette, a free arrangement), look at the result with ui_screenshot once and fix what's off (unreadable text, a panel over the scene's focus); it also shows you what the user means by "that thing at the top", and when no setting does what they ask, say so and offer the nearest one instead. For anything finer than a setting, any single element however small ("move the send button over a bit", "make that label red", "hide the token count", "put a clock next to the model name", "a button that says hi"), use ui_fluid: inspect first (under the part they mean, or find by its text) to get the element's path, then set or insert. Prefer it over saying something can't be changed. When a message says an element was selected on screen in edit mode, that's the element they mean.
